sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Liverpool host Fulham at Anfield with Liverpool 5th (49 points) and Fulham 10th (44). Sofascore’s model leans to the hosts (home win 55%, draw 23%, away win 22) and suggests a decent chance both teams score (58%).

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Liverpool are 1-1-3 across their last 5, including heavy defeats at Manchester City (0-4) and Paris Saint-Germain (0-2), but they dominated Galatasaray at home. Fulham are 2-1-2, rebounding with a 3-1 win over Burnley after tight 0-1 losses to West Ham and Southampton and a 0-0 at Nottingham Forest.

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: The last 2 meetings at Craven Cottage produced goals for both sides (2-2 on 04 Jan 2026; 3-2 Fulham on 06 Apr 2025). Trend-wise, both teams have scored in 7/7 recent head-to-heads and over 2.5 goals has landed in 6/7.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and playing styles
sections.text: Liverpool’s season profile points to front-foot football: 60% average possession (league rank 1), 82 big chances created (rank 6) but a low 33% conversion (rank 18). Set-piece and delivery output is steady (6.0 corners per game, rank 4), and they are strong in the air (55% aerials, rank 2), while defensive numbers show room for improvement (42 conceded).

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: For Liverpool, Dominik Szoboszlai is in form (last 5: 7.52 rating, 2 goals), with Mohamed Salah contributing 5 goals and 6 assists. Fulham’s Harry Wilson remains a live threat (10 goals, 6 assists; player of the match in the last head-to-head), while Raúl Jiménez adds penalty-box presence (9 goals).

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Anthony Taylor averages 3.8 yellows and 0.18 reds per game. Recent head-to-heads have tended to stay under on cards, while Liverpool’s corner output (≈6 per game) and Fulham’s recent patterns point to a near double-digit total.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Liverpool’s superior possession, chance creation and Anfield advantage align with the model’s edge to the hosts. Given head-to-head trends and the 58% both-teams-to-score signal, expect Liverpool to edge a competitive match with both sides creating.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool lead 2-0 at half-time at Anfield after goals from Rio Ngumoha (36') and Mohamed Salah (40'). The hosts have controlled most phases with cleaner shot quality and more sustained territory. Fulham have had moments on the break but have not created a clear chance.

halftimeSections.subtitle: First-half summary
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool held more of the ball and produced the better chances (possession 60-40, expected goals 1.03-0.17, shots on target 4-3). They progressed consistently (final third entries 23-13, penalty area entries 14-7) and pressed effectively high up (possessions won in the final third 6-1). Fulham won more duels and aerials (duels won 62% to 38%, aerials 55% to 45%), but this did not translate into chance quality. Liverpool’s big moments came via Salah and Ngumoha, with supply from Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo, each credited with an assist.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Attack momentum
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool started on the front foot with a long opening spell of pressure. Fulham then enjoyed their best sequence around the half-hour, forcing Liverpool deeper for several minutes. Liverpool responded before the interval with another strong attacking wave, during which they scored and then continued to threaten up to the break.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key players and match-ups
halftimeSections.text: Mohamed Salah was decisive with 1 goal and consistent shot threat, while Rio Ngumoha provided a composed finish and direct running. Florian Wirtz created well between the lines with multiple key passes. Andrew Robertson supported attacks from deep with one effort on target. For Fulham, Sander Berge’s ball-winning kept them competitive in midfield, while Alex Iwobi and Oscar Bobb tested the goalkeeper with efforts from transitional moments. Joachim Andersen’s effort on target underlined set-piece potential, but Fulham lacked a clear big chance for Rodrigo Muniz.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical outlook for second half
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool can manage the game with controlled possession and selective pressing. With space likely to open, quick diagonals into Salah and Ngumoha, plus overlaps from Jeremie Frimpong and Robertson, should continue to create chances. Fulham need earlier forward connections and more consistent wide overloads. Bringing Harry Wilson and Iwobi closer to Muniz and pushing Antonee Robinson and Timothy Castagne higher could improve crossing volume. Set-pieces remain Fulham’s most viable route back if they cannot break Liverpool’s first line.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Discipline, cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: No cards have been shown so far. Corners are 2-1 to Liverpool. Expect a low to moderate card count after the interval if Fulham chase the game, with 1-3 cautions likely. Corners should rise as Fulham push up; anticipate roughly 4-6 second-half corners, with Liverpool likely to edge the count given their territorial play.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: Liverpool are favoured to score the next goal given their chance quality and territorial control. Fulham may create from set-pieces or transitions, but Liverpool’s structure and pressing numbers point to a controlled finish. Predicted outcome: Liverpool to add once more and close it out at 3-0, with Salah the most likely scorer early in the half.
